summary: Ground cabin on Weyerhaeuser land in Klamath County: summit firefinder c.1932, 9x9-ft cabin built 1949, last staffed 1966, abandoned and barely standing at a June 2025 visit.

facts.design: 9x9-ft wooden cab built 1949; a 1953 Coast and Geodetic Survey recovery note describes a 9x9-ft house on a group of large boulders at the summit
facts.status_note: Abandoned after 1966. A June 2025 visit found the cabin deteriorating and barely standing; firelookout.com says it is still there.

access.note: On Weyerhaeuser Company land; a 1965 Weyerhaeuser permit covered the association's installations. No current public-access rule was found.

events.note: Firefinder on the summit with a cabin lower down, per two sources. The NHLR instead says the 1949 house replaced an earlier structure dating to at least 1930.
A newspaper item credits the Bear Flat lookout with sighting a fire near Wednesday night and extinguishing it.
The lookout reported a fire that had burned about four acres on the Klamath Indian Reservation.
Current 9x9-ft wooden cab; the lookout house was constructed at a cost of $177.83.
Coast and Geodetic Survey station recovery note describes a small 9x9-ft house on a group of large boulders at the summit.
Electricity installed for radio, lights and heating.
Weyerhaeuser granted the KFPA a permit to construct, operate and maintain existing installations.
Last staffed in 1966; the Forest Lookouts page says it was not permanently manned that season.
Firelookout.com says the cabin was abandoned in 1966.
Registered June 22, 2022; nominated by Brad Eells.
June 2025 visit report: cabin deteriorating and barely standing.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 5,503 ft (1,677 m); firelookout.com gives 5527 ft. The record keeps the NHLR figure.
The NHLR says the 1949 house replaced a structure dating to at least 1930. Firelookout.com and the 2025 visit report date the summit firefinder and lower cabin to about 1932. The story reports both.

The 2025 visit report lists the type as a 20-ft steel tower. Firelookout.com describes a 9x9-ft wooden cab, and a 1953 Coast and Geodetic Survey recovery note describes a 9x9-ft house; the NHLR gives no type. The story follows the cabin description.

notes_for_editor: Access 'permission' is inferred from Weyerhaeuser land ownership and the 1965 permit; no current access rule was found, and the story gives no visiting directions. The 2025 visit report calls the cabin abandoned and barely standing and describes a bushwhack, so the record's status keeps 'standing' with a status note. The 2025 report lists a 20-ft steel tower, which conflicts with the cabin in other sources; check the type before using 'design'. A 1935 US Forest Service recovery note places the station at the center of the lookout house but gives no size. The 1953 Coast and Geodetic Survey note may describe an earlier house rather than the 1949 cabin. The record's elevation (1677.3 m) follows the NHLR figure.
